userStories.title: KB route writes are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Record the four KB route writes after successful store calls without changing permissions, ownership checks or responses.

**Motivation** — P1 closed the permission side; the Audit log is the only place that shows who replaced what, and when.

**Approach** — Relevant design calls reproduced verbatim:

- **A KB write records after the LanceDB write succeeds.** KB documents live in the LanceDB table, which has no transaction to share with `AuditEntry`. `RagController` runs the store call first and then `this.audit.audited(async () => undefined, () => entries)`, a transaction holding only the entries. A failed store call records nothing. A `record` that rejects after a successful store call leaves the KB change in place and the route answers an error status. Recording first (the `fleet.knowledge.repo.reindex` order) would leave an entry for a write that then failed; holding a Postgres transaction open across an embedding call would hit Prisma's 5 s interactive-transaction timeout.
- **A graphify import records after the import, the same way.** `RagService.importGraphify` writes the graph in `PrismaRagRepository.applyGraphDiff`'s own `$transaction` and the LanceDB rows outside it, then stamps `graphifyLastImportedAt`. The route records `kb.graphify.import` after `importGraphify` resolves. An empty `nodes` list returns before any write and records nothing, as today.
- **A KB delete records one entry per source that had rows, right after that source's delete.** `DELETE …/kb/documents/:sourceId` without `source` deletes both user sources (`doc`, `manual`). The route already reads each source's creators before deleting. In its loop, after each `deleteBySource` resolves for a source with at least one row, it records `kb.document.delete` through `audited`; a source with none records nothing. So a second source's failure leaves the first source's delete with its entry.
- **`projectId` is the row's project.** The KB route's project, the memory item's `projectId`, the governed project, the code-intel route's project.

Summary/resource contract (verbatim relevant rows):
| Write | Key | `resourceType` | `resourceId` | `projectId` | `summary` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| KB document added | `kb.document.add` | `kb-document` | `<source>:<sourceId>` | the project | `added <source> document` |
| KB document rows deleted (per source with rows) | `kb.document.delete` | `kb-document` | `<source>:<sourceId>` | the project | `deleted <n> <source> rows` |
| graphify import | `kb.graphify.import` | `project` | the project id | the project | `imported <n> nodes, cleared <m>` |
| KB table optimized | `kb.optimize` | `project` | the project id | the project | `kb table optimized` |

`<source>` is `doc` or `manual`; `<n>` is the number of rows the source had before the delete (the length of `findSourceCreators`' answer). `<n>` and `<m>` of the import are `importGraphify`'s `imported` and `cleared`. Never include content, metadata, graphify labels or files in summaries. Routes use the ambient request actor, origin rest; do not manufacture context. Keep all source ownership preflight checks before either delete.

**Scope** — In: RagController constructor injection and four write handlers; create test/integration/audit/audit-kb-routes.integration.spec.ts; adapt recorder providers in src/rag/rag.controller.spec.ts, src/projects/project-membership.guard.routes.spec.ts, src/rag/kb-documents-membership.routes.spec.ts, test/integration/graphify-kb-validation/graphify-kb-validation.integration.spec.ts and test/integration/rag/rag-api-project-id-validation.integration.spec.ts, retaining existing assertions. Out: memory hooks/routes (US-002), memory tools/system writers (US-003), AST indexing (US-004). Preserve the following feature-level boundaries here too:
- Making a KB write and its entry atomic is out of scope: LanceDB has no transaction to share, so the entry is written after the store call and a failed `record` leaves the KB change in place.
- Recording the derived indexes (`KbTicketLifecycleSubscriber`, `EntityGraphOutboxSubscriber`, the `system.rag.optimize` strategies, `RagModule`'s `graphify_import` handler) and a push's `removeFiles` is out of scope; the write each derives from carries the entry.
- US-001 only: a test of a delete whose second source's `deleteBySource` throws is out of scope; the per-source record order is pinned by AC6.
- US-001 only: a separate test of a rejected `record` after a delete, a graphify import or an optimize is out of scope; each is the same record-after-the-store-call step AC4 pins for an add.
Preserve those runtime contracts by per-source order and the common post-store mechanism; the failure-table assertions for these expressly test-deferred cases are reviewable contracts, not instructions to add the excluded tests.

**Interface** — Existing read-only store signatures: `RagService.indexDocument(projectId, doc): Promise<string | null>`, `deleteBySource`, `findSourceCreators`, `importGraphify(projectId, nodes, links): Promise<{ imported; cleared }>`, `optimizeTable`. Use existing `AuditRecorder.record(input)` and `AuditRecorder.audited(fn, entriesOf)` (`entriesOf` may return `[]`), `AuditRecordInput { key; resourceType; resourceId; projectId?; summary? }`.

- **`AuditRecorder` is a required constructor dependency, last.** `RagController`, `MemoryController`, `MemoryWriteTools`, `MemoryOutboxSubscriber`, `MemoryGovernanceProcessor` and `CodeIntelController` take it as their new last parameter. `CodeIntelOutboxSubscriber` takes it right after `registry`, before its two `@Optional()` parameters. `addMemoryTool` and `recordDecisionTool` take it as a new `audit` field of their `deps`.

Validation: use three-session-tdd because ownership/access-control regression paths are involved. Boot real AppModule with bootHttpApp({ registrationEnabled: false }), project kb-audit/KBA, root Owner and dev developer; use EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=fake before boot and restore it, resetThrottle beforeEach, and fixtureDb audit reads plus RagService.listDocuments. New audit integration tests use the real recorder; unrelated constructor/DI tests use mockAuditRecorder. Add the null-index unit case to rag.controller.spec.ts. Follow the shared analysis's fixtures, keyed audit-down spy and DB execution guidance.

userStories.title: Memory tools, outbox extraction and governance are audited
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit both memory tools, outbox-extracted memories and changed-project governance runs with their correct ambient tool or system context.

**Motivation** — A KB document a Developer replaced, a memory fact an agent superseded through MCP, a decision a thread recorded on approval and a nightly cleanup that expired a project's memory still leave no entry.

**Approach** — Relevant design calls reproduced verbatim:

- **A tool entry carries the tool's context.** Through MCP the actor is the agent, origin `mcp` (`directWrite`). Through a thread approval `AssistantToolExecutor.executeAction` runs the tool as `SYSTEM/assistant` on behalf of the requester (`onBehalfOf` `{ type: 'USER', id }`), origin `thread`, with the action's approval block (`assistant-tool.executor.ts:104`), and `record` copies all three. `MemoryWriteTools` passes its injected `AuditRecorder` to both tool factories.
- **The outbox extraction records as `SYSTEM/memory`.** Fan-out handlers run inside `runAsSystem('outbox')` (`fan-out-publisher.ts:75`). `MemoryOutboxSubscriber`'s two handlers run their body inside `runAsSystemWriter(this, …)` (`system.memory.extract-from-event` → `memory`), so the item and its entry are the memory component's; `runAsSystem` inherits the outbox record's `correlationId`. This follows audit-fleet-system's call "an entry under a `system.*` key always carries that component's actor".
- **Governance records one entry per project per run that changed rows.** `MemoryGovernanceService.runCleanup` makes one small write per item outside any transaction, and wrapping a whole project's cleanup in one transaction would risk the timeout. `MemoryGovernanceProcessor.cleanUpAllProjects` records `system.memory.govern` on the project after `runCleanup` resolves, through `audited(async () => result, entriesOf)` with `entriesOf` returning `[]` when all four counts are 0. A rejected `record` lands in the existing per-project `catch`: logged, the next project runs, and the run throws its summary error at the end, as for any cleanup failure today.
- **`AuditRecorder` is a required constructor dependency, last.** `RagController`, `MemoryController`, `MemoryWriteTools`, `MemoryOutboxSubscriber`, `MemoryGovernanceProcessor` and `CodeIntelController` take it as their new last parameter. `CodeIntelOutboxSubscriber` takes it right after `registry`, before its two `@Optional()` parameters. `addMemoryTool` and `recordDecisionTool` take it as a new `audit` field of their `deps`.

Summary/resource contract (verbatim relevant rows):
| Write | Key | `resourceType` | `resourceId` | `projectId` | `summary` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| memory item via `POST /memory` or `koda_add_memory` | `memory.create` | `memory-item` | the new item's id | the item's project | `memoryWriteSummary` |
| decision via `POST /memory/decisions` or `koda_record_decision` | `memory.decision.record` | `memory-item` | the new item's id | the item's project | `memoryWriteSummary` |
| memory item from an outbox event | `system.memory.extract-from-event` | `memory-item` | the new item's id | the item's project | `memoryWriteSummary` |
| governance cleanup that changed rows | `system.memory.govern` | `project` | the project id | the project | `expired <a>, downranked <b>, deduplicated <c>, superseded <d>` |

`<a>`..`<d>` are `GovernanceResult`'s four counts. Use expiredCount, downrankedCount, deduplicatedCount and supersessionCount in that order. Tool writes use onWritten: memoryAuditHook(deps.audit, 'memory.create') or memoryAuditHook(deps.audit, 'memory.decision.record') alongside beforeSupersede; the two outbox handler bodies use runAsSystemWriter and persistExtractedItems passes { onWritten: memoryAuditHook(this.audit, 'system.memory.extract-from-event') }. Do not set actor, approval or onBehalfOf in tools: approved actions already carry USER onBehalfOf, and agent direct thread writes already carry AGENT onBehalfOf; record copies them. Outbox extraction has no event-actor onBehalfOf. Keep parse, preview, owner attribution, source fields, refusal mapping, extraction and handler registration unchanged. Hook failure rolls back the item's upsert and propagates through the existing tool/fan-out failure path.

**Scope** — In: add-memory-tool.ts, record-decision-tool.ts, memory-write-tools.ts, memory-outbox.subscriber.ts and memory-governance.processor.ts; create test/integration/audit/audit-memory-system.integration.spec.ts; update tool specs, origin-tools.spec.ts, subscriber/processor unit specs, outbox-envelope.integration.spec.ts direct construction and outbox-fanout-extraction.integration.spec.ts providers/mocks, retaining existing assertions. Out: creation of memoryAuditHook/onWritten and REST route changes (US-002), KB route auditing (US-001), code-intel auditing (US-004). Preserve these nearby feature boundaries:
- Wrapping a project's governance cleanup in one transaction is out of scope; its entry is written after the cleanup resolves.
- An `onBehalfOf` on the outbox extraction's entries (the event's actor) is out of scope; the shared `correlationId` joins them.
- The delivery integrations (outbound webhooks and delivery, skills, notifications and ticket watch, outbox, email, fleet health, the assistant action finalize, the role seeder, the remaining assistant tools) are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-delivery`).
The outbox exclusion refers to the outbox infrastructure/delivery writers, not this story's explicitly included MemoryOutboxSubscriber handler bodies.

**Interface** — Upstream US-002 provides:
```typescript
export interface MemoryWritten {
  item: MemoryItem;
  superseded: MemoryItem | null;
}
export type MemoryAuditKey = 'memory.create' | 'memory.extract' | 'memory.decision.record' | 'system.memory.extract-from-event';
export function memoryWriteSummary(written: MemoryWritten): string;
export function memoryAuditHook(audit: AuditRecorder, key: MemoryAuditKey): (written: MemoryWritten) => Promise<void>;
```

Changed factory contracts (verbatim): `addMemoryTool(deps: { memory; guard })` and `recordDecisionTool(deps: { memory; extraction; guard })` → each `deps` gains `audit: AuditRecorder`. `MemoryUpsertOptions` accepts `onWritten?: (written: MemoryWritten) => Promise<void>`. Existing `MemoryGovernanceService.runCleanup(projectId): Promise<GovernanceResult>` is unchanged.

Validation: three-session-tdd for tool authorization/approval-context paths. Boot real AppModule with project mem-sys/MSY, fake embeddings, MCP_ENABLED=true before boot and an agent developer key; restore flags in afterAll and resetThrottle beforeEach. Exercise both tools by MCP tools/call; publish real ticket_event outbox records under SYSTEM/outbox and invoke scheduledCleanup through DI. Assert persisted AuditEntry and memory rows. Unit tool stubs must invoke onWritten and assert their exact keys, pinning the approval execute seam without a new thread-approval harness. Unit outbox stubs capture currentContext and options. Governance recorder stub must evaluate entriesOf and call record, including a p-1 failure followed by successful p-2 recording. Keep module compilation DB-free using GlobalStubsModule/mockAuditRecorder; fixture mocks that actually call the real repository need withTransaction after US-002. For the failure-table lastError assertion only, persist an outboxEvent row and pass its id via outboxRecord's overrides; outboxRecord alone creates an in-memory envelope, and recordLastError is a no-op for a missing row. Keep the numbered integration ACs' real FanOutPublisher path; do not introduce a new publisher or retry loop. Follow shared analysis's host-only DB rules and exact failure spy.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Audit REST and push-driven symbol indexing inside the existing index transaction with request or codeintel-system context.

**Motivation** — P1 closed the permission side; the Audit log is the only place that shows who replaced what, and when.

**Approach** — Relevant design calls reproduced verbatim:

- **The code-intel route records inside the index transaction.** `AstIndexService.indexCommit` already runs its deletes and upserts in one `txManager.run` (`ast-index.service.ts:89`). It gains an optional last parameter `onIndexed?: (result: { symbolsIndexed: number; filesIndexed: number }) => Promise<void>`, awaited inside that `run` after the last upsert, and only when `files` was not empty (a file that fails to parse still has its old symbols deleted, so it counts as a write; `files: []` writes nothing and records nothing). `CodeIntelController.indexCommit` passes a callback that records `codeintel.index.write`.
- **The push-driven commit index records once per indexed commit.** A push's `code_commit` outbox rows are bookkeeping (audit-vcs-ci), so nothing upstream records the symbols a push writes. `CodeCommitOutboxHandler.process` gains an optional last parameter `onIndexed`, forwarded to `indexCommit` as its fifth argument. `CodeIntelOutboxSubscriber.handleCodeCommit` runs inside `runAsSystemWriter(this, …)` (`system.codeintel.index-commit` → `codeintel`) and passes a callback that records `system.codeintel.index-commit`, on both its handler path and its direct `astIndexService.indexCommit` fallback. A commit with no files to index, no connection or no key records nothing. Removing a commit's deleted files (`removeFiles`) is bookkeeping. This follows audit-fleet-system's "a knowledge pass records once, when it completes".
- **`AuditRecorder` is a required constructor dependency, last.** `RagController`, `MemoryController`, `MemoryWriteTools`, `MemoryOutboxSubscriber`, `MemoryGovernanceProcessor` and `CodeIntelController` take it as their new last parameter. `CodeIntelOutboxSubscriber` takes it right after `registry`, before its two `@Optional()` parameters. `addMemoryTool` and `recordDecisionTool` take it as a new `audit` field of their `deps`.

Baseline-to-target clarification: CodeCommitOutboxHandler does not originate an audit callback; it forwards the optional onIndexed supplied by the subscriber, and forwards undefined when called without one. This preserves four-argument indexCommit callers while satisfying the specified push integration criteria. The spec's baseline statement that the handler passes none is superseded by its explicit changed interface and push acceptance criteria.

Summary/resource contract (verbatim relevant rows):
| Write | Key | `resourceType` | `resourceId` | `projectId` | `summary` |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| code-intel index | `codeintel.index.write` | `code-repo` | the request's `repoId` | the project | `indexed <s> symbols in <f> files` |
| commit indexed from a push | `system.codeintel.index-commit` | `code-repo` | the payload's `repoId` | the payload's `projectId` | `indexed <s> symbols in <f> files` |

`<s>` and `<f>` are `symbolsIndexed` and `filesIndexed`. Never include source paths/content, symbol names or commit hashes. REST uses its request actor, origin rest. Push runs as SYSTEM/codeintel, origin system, inheriting correlationId. Keep parsing, deletion/upsert order, relationship resolution, replace-not-merge behavior, result and route response unchanged; record failure rolls back the index transaction so prior symbols survive and no new symbols remain. Do not audit an empty file list, but do invoke onIndexed for a nonempty parse-failing file because deleting its old symbols is still a write. Keep VCS fetch outside the transaction and preserve existing handler/fallback skips.

**Scope** — In: ast-index.service.ts, code-intel.controller.ts, code-commit-outbox-handler.ts, code-intel-outbox.subscriber.ts; create test/integration/audit/audit-code-intel.integration.spec.ts. Adapt code-intel.controller.spec.ts and both modules in code-intel-search.controller.spec.ts for the required recorder; add AST callback-in-transaction, backward-compatibility and empty-list unit cases. Adapt subscriber direct constructors and exact process/indexCommit assertions; add callback-context and forwarding unit cases in subscriber/handler specs. Adapt code-commit-outbox-handler.removed-files.spec.ts and test/integration/ast-index/code-commit-handler.integration.spec.ts while preserving old assertions. Out: KB routes (US-001), memory repository/routes (US-002), memory tools/system writers (US-003), VCS connection auditing or credential changes. Preserve these nearby feature boundaries:
- Recording the derived indexes (`KbTicketLifecycleSubscriber`, `EntityGraphOutboxSubscriber`, the `system.rag.optimize` strategies, `RagModule`'s `graphify_import` handler) and a push's `removeFiles` is out of scope; the write each derives from carries the entry.
- The runtime coverage guard and the walker test over write surfaces are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-coverage`). The Bookkeeping table is its input.
- US-004 only: tests of a push with no files to index, no VCS connection or no encryption key are out of scope; those early returns are unchanged and never reach `indexCommit`.
Retain those runtime paths and review their unchanged skips instead; their failure-table assertions do not require the expressly excluded tests.

**Interface** — Changed signature (verbatim): `AstIndexService.indexCommit(repoId, commitHash, files, projectId)` → `indexCommit(repoId, commitHash, files, projectId, onIndexed?: (result: { symbolsIndexed: number; filesIndexed: number }) => Promise<void>)`. `CodeCommitOutboxHandler.process` gains an optional last `onIndexed` parameter with that same count-pair callback type and forwards it as indexCommit's fifth argument. CodeIntelController requires AuditRecorder last; CodeIntelOutboxSubscriber requires it immediately after registry and before its two @Optional parameters.

Validation: three-session-tdd because this touches a permission-gated write and system attribution. Boot real AppModule with project ci-intel/CIN, root Owner and viewer; fake embedding provider before boot for any ticket fixtures. Set VCS_ENCRYPTION_KEY='ab'.repeat(32) before boot and restore it, create the specified GitHub webhook connection, and partially mock src/vcs/factory preserving other exports. Exercise the index route over HTTP and actual FanOutPublisher code_commit publication under SYSTEM/outbox; query AuditEntry through fixtureDb and symbols over HTTP. The route callback rollback case must prove alpha survives and beta does not; push rollback must prove pushedTwo is absent. Unit txManager.run flag proves onIndexed executes before commit. Existing four-argument callers still return their usual result and process(payload) forwards undefined. For the failure-table lastError assertion only, persist an outboxEvent row and pass its id via outboxRecord's overrides; a synthetic envelope with no stored row cannot prove lastError persistence. The numbered push ACs still enter through the real FanOutPublisher; do not add a retry loop or change outbox infrastructure. Use the analysis's keyed record-down spy, environment restoration, throttler reset and host DB guidance.

RISKS AND MIGRATION
Primary risks are accidentally recording outside shared transaction ALS, rollback regressions when replacing an item/symbol set, duplicate replay audit rows, incorrect system/outbox identity, lost thread approval/onBehalfOf, leaked user-written content, no-op entries, constructor DI breakage and unintentionally changing permission checks or HTTP contracts. Mitigate with the prescribed transaction callbacks, context wrappers, count/no-op assertions, existing permission suites and real AppModule row reads. No backfill or database migration: deploy the additive caller hooks and required DI wiring together. Existing callers without onIndexed/onWritten remain supported; addMemoryTool/recordDecisionTool and constructor call sites require explicit dependency updates. Existing audit rows are unchanged and only future successful writes gain entries. LanceDB and governance mutations can remain committed when auditing fails; preserve this intentional non-atomic failure contract rather than hiding it or adding compensating writes.
outOfScope: The delivery integrations (outbound webhooks and delivery, skills, notifications and ticket watch, outbox, email, fleet health, the assistant action finalize, the role seeder, the remaining assistant tools) are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-delivery`).
The runtime coverage guard and the walker test over write surfaces are out of scope (feature `permissions-p2-audit-coverage`). The Bookkeeping table is its input.

Recording the derived indexes (`KbTicketLifecycleSubscriber`, `EntityGraphOutboxSubscriber`, the `system.rag.optimize` strategies, `RagModule`'s `graphify_import` handler) and a push's `removeFiles` is out of scope; the write each derives from carries the entry.
The fleet knowledge routes, `KnowledgeRepoIndexer` passes and `KnowledgePoller` are out of scope; audit-fleet-ops and audit-fleet-system settled them.
Making a KB write and its entry atomic is out of scope: LanceDB has no transaction to share, so the entry is written after the store call and a failed `record` leaves the KB change in place.
Wrapping a project's governance cleanup in one transaction is out of scope; its entry is written after the cleanup resolves.
Recording a memory read, a KB search, a context query, a timeline read or a code-intel read is out of scope; only committed writes are recorded.
Recording refused or failed attempts (401, 403, 404, 409, validation errors) is out of scope.
Adding catalog keys (one per memory kind, one for a replacement) is out of scope; each write records under its existing key and the summary names the kind and the superseded id.

Changing a route's status codes, response bodies or `@Requires` keys, the replace and delete checks, the memory dedup key, the Serializable isolation or the KB row ownership rules is out of scope; `openapi.json` does not change.

A retry of a Serializable conflict (`P2034`) in `upsert` is out of scope; a conflict, like any Prisma error inside `upsert`, now surfaces through `PrismaService.withTransaction`'s error mapping (`P2002` as a 409, an unmapped code such as `P2034` as a 500).
An `onBehalfOf` on the outbox extraction's entries (the event's actor) is out of scope; the shared `correlationId` joins them.
A before/after diff of values in `AuditEntry` is out of scope.
